teaching.hint: At one depth, which position in a left-to-right traversal corresponds to the node that blocks all others from the right?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Exactly one node per depth is visible: the rightmost node at that level.
solution_outline.approach: Traverse breadth-first one level at a time, enqueueing each left child before its right child, and append the final node processed from each level.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The queue holds each level in left-to-right order; the final processed node in the current level is therefore its rightmost node.
solution_outline.correctness: Left-before-right enqueuing preserves left-to-right order at every subsequent depth. Thus the final node of each processed level is exactly the visible node for that depth, and collecting these levels top-down returns the required view.
solution_outline.complexity: Every node is visited once, giving O(n) time and O(w) auxiliary queue space for maximum width w.
solution_outline.pitfall: Returning only nodes that have no right child mistakes a structural property for rightmost position; a left child can be visible.

accepted_alternatives: Depth-first traversal that visits right children before left children and records the first node reached at each depth.
common_wrong_turns: Ignoring visible left children when no right child exists
Appending every last child encountered without grouping by depth
Returning node values in bottom-up order
source_fidelity_notes: Illustrated examples were omitted; view direction, top-down order, empty-tree behavior, and node and value bounds were retained.
